## Conference overview

*Preview by Adam Burke, p. 317. Reproduced in full.*


> The Sun Belt remains the only conference in college football to still use divisions, as the 14 teams in the conference are split right down the middle to form the East and West.

> Traditionally, the East has been stronger with teams like App State and Coastal Carolina and only got stronger when James Madison and Marshall joined the conference.

> The West is headlined primarily by Louisiana and Troy, but Louisiana Tech is a conference newcomer this season looking to make some noise.

> Texas State jumped ship to join the reimagined Pac-12.

> Conference favorite James Madison has experienced big changes once again, as Bob Chesney followed predecessor Curt Cignetti to the Big Ten.

> Billy Napier, lovingly (sort of) referred to as “Sun Belt Billy” for his time at Louisiana, is back in the conference now after falling short of expectations at Florida.

> Incredibly, he is one of just three new head coaches in the conference, as we usually see a lot of turnover in the Sun Belt and similar leagues.

> The others are Ryan Beard at Coastal Carolina and Blake Anderson, another former Sun Belt boss, at Southern Miss.

> This is a conference that is important to know because of the early-season weeknight games across the ESPN family of networks, so you’re going to get a few standalone Sun Belt nights where those teams are front and center before we really get into the NBA and NHL seasons.

> There can be some excellent betting opportunities for those who are keeping tabs on the conference.

> Of course, the carrot of the College Football Playoff berth that dangles in front of the highest-ranked G6 conference champ is something that adds intrigue to the season.

> Last year, it was James Madison who locked that up and put forth a decent effort against Oregon, covering the 21-point number in a 17-point loss.

> The Dukes are +270 to run it back in the “Fun Belt”, but they are +1500 to make the CFP for a second straight year.

> Old Dominion is the second shot at +460 before we get to Louisiana (7-1) and Troy (8-1), so the East looks to be outpacing the West yet again. sun belt

## Quarterback themes


**From the conference preview (p. 317):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 14 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Appalachian State Mountaineers** (p. 318) — Per 247Sports, App State reeled in the secondranked transfer portal class, including a few new options at QB, and the top freshman class in the conference.

- **Arkansas State Red Wolves** (p. 332) — We’ll see what kind of fortunes the Red Wolves have this season, as they’ll play without QB Jaylen Raynor for the first time since 2022, a season in which they finished 3-9.

- **Coastal Carolina Chanticleers** (p. 320) — All of the quarterbacks that Beard brought in have eligibility past this season.

- **Georgia Southern Eagles** (p. 323) — All-time leading passer JC French transferred to Cincinnati after posting a 20/8 TD/INT ratio with 2,929 yards and six more touchdowns on the ground.

- **Georgia State Panthers** (p. 324) — Injuries didn’t help, especially at the QB position, where Cameran Brown is and was clearly the best option.

- **James Madison Dukes** (p. 326) — They do have resources, but Curt Cignetti and Bob Chesney have done a masterful job of finding talent, especially at the QB position.

- **Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns** (p. 334) — The fact that he was a Ragin’ Cajun QB from 2005-08 probably adds some leeway, but Louisiana has three 6-7 seasons on his watch and one 10-4 season that ended with a 31-3 loss in the conference title game and then a 34-3 loss in the bowl game.

- **Louisiana Tech Bulldogs** (p. 339) — The Bulldogs defense actually allowed fewer points per game (20.8 to 21) with first-year DC Luke Olsen, but allowed 0.6 more yards per carry, 67 more passing yards per game, and 0.7 more yards per play.

## Returning-production themes


**From the conference preview (p. 317):**

> Conference favorite James Madison has experienced big changes once again, as Bob Chesney followed predecessor Curt Cignetti to the Big Ten.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 317*

> Billy Napier, lovingly (sort of) referred to as “Sun Belt Billy” for his time at Louisiana, is back in the conference now after falling short of expectations at Florida.

**From the team pages in this conference** — 13 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Appalachian State Mountaineers** (p. 318) — The boys from Boone have had back-to-back five-win seasons, an unacceptable outcome for a team that has won 10+ games in a season four times over the last decade.

- **Arkansas State Red Wolves** (p. 332) — But, Raynor also leaves at the same time as all-time leading receiver Corey Rucker, so there is a ton of offensive production to replace.

- **Coastal Carolina Chanticleers** (p. 320) — While Beck led the Chants to an 8-5 record in Year 1, backto-back losing seasons sent him packing and now Ryan Beard has been tabbed to lead the program.

- **Georgia Southern Eagles** (p. 323) — Both Josh Dallas and River Helms were lost for the season early and are back.

- **Georgia State Panthers** (p. 324) — OC Hue Jackson is back, but the co-DCs are new as McGee probably needs a decent season to save his job.

- **James Madison Dukes** (p. 326) — With NIL funds allocated elsewhere, the Dukes didn’t go the transfer portal route at QB, really, with the exception of UCF transfer Davi Belfort, who barely played. 247Sports gave James Madison’s portal haul the best grade in the conference by a pretty wide margin, which is good because pretty much all of last season’s production is gone, but a lot of players are from lower-division schools, FCS, or never saw the field at their P4 programs.

- **Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns** (p. 334) — He got a five-year extension after the 10-4 season, but reverted right back to what he was doing prior to that year.

- **Marshall Thundering Herd** (p. 329) — The defense took a massive step back last season for Marshall, but the offense was nearly as good as the season prior.

## Transfer-portal themes


**From the conference preview (p. 317):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 12 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Appalachian State Mountaineers** (p. 318) — Per 247Sports, App State reeled in the secondranked transfer portal class, including a few new options at QB, and the top freshman class in the conference.

- **Coastal Carolina Chanticleers** (p. 320) — This is a taller task now, especially with about 60 new players in the mix, including a conference-high 42 transfers per 247Sports.

- **Georgia Southern Eagles** (p. 323) — All-time leading passer JC French transferred to Cincinnati after posting a 20/8 TD/INT ratio with 2,929 yards and six more touchdowns on the ground.

- **Georgia State Panthers** (p. 325) — A guy like McGee makes sense on paper, but he doesn’t have a big NIL budget and that’s what you need with this kind of head coach.

- **James Madison Dukes** (p. 326) — No team in the Sun Belt has been able to leverage the transfer portal better than James Madison.

- **Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns** (p. 334) — The Ragin’ Cajuns enter this season with the fewest portal additions in the conference, so either there’s not much money there or nobody’s willing to invest money.

- **Marshall Thundering Herd** (p. 328) — On the other hand, a 5-7 team didn’t really get any better via the portal or the freshman class based on their conference ranking.

- **Old Dominion Monarchs** (p. 330) — These whiplash sorts of seasons are very possible at the G6 level nowadays thanks to the portal, as some teams get completely wrecked and others stay intact enough to take advantage.

## Schedule themes


**From the conference preview (p. 317):**

> *Not addressed in guide.*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 8 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Appalachian State Mountaineers** (p. 318) — App State plays at the highest elevation east of the Mississippi River in FBS and using that to their advantage makes a ton of sense, if Loggains and the new-look offense are able to achieve that.

- **Arkansas State Red Wolves** (p. 332) — All SBC road games are winnable, including the one against conference favorite Louisiana, and drawing Coastal Carolina and Georgia State from the East is a boost to the team’s forecast.

- **Georgia Southern Eagles** (p. 322) — This is tough because the Over 4.5 is juicy, but six wins is a challenge with the schedule.

- **Georgia State Panthers** (p. 324) — It’s a rough schedule with a bad team and probably a lame-duck head coach.

- **James Madison Dukes** (p. 326) — The schedule includes a long trip west to San Diego State, a random non-conference roadie at UConn, and road games at Old Dominion and App State.

- **Louisiana Tech Bulldogs** (p. 338) — The West Division is the weaker of the two in the Sun Belt, but it is an objectively stronger conference on the whole and Baylor joins LSU on the non-conference schedule.

- **Marshall Thundering Herd** (p. 328) — On the plus side, Carlos Del Rio-Wilson found a home after bouncing around a bit and enough players bought in to the point where they’ve stuck around.

- **Old Dominion Monarchs** (p. 330) — One of the six games came against Old Dominion, who was badly outgained in the regularseason opener, but lost 27-14 in what turned out to be a sign of things to come.

## Historical and situational notes


**From the conference preview (p. 317):**

> Last year, it was James Madison who locked that up and put forth a decent effort against Oregon, covering the 21-point number in a 17-point loss.
>
> — *conference preview, p. 317*


**From the team pages in this conference** — 14 of 14 teams' pages address this theme. A sample follows; Phase 3 carries the full treatment team by team.


- **Appalachian State Mountaineers** (p. 318) — The boys from Boone have had back-to-back five-win seasons, an unacceptable outcome for a team that has won 10+ games in a season four times over the last decade.

- **Arkansas State Red Wolves** (p. 332) — It took a couple of seasons for Butch Jones to pick up the pieces in Jonesboro coming out of COVID and the end of Blake Anderson’s tenure, but the program has gone to a bowl game three seasons in a row and has their first winning streak in bowl games since 2012-13 under Gus Malzahn and Bryan Harsin.

- **Coastal Carolina Chanticleers** (p. 320) — Beard oversaw Missouri State’s transition from FCS to FBS and got the Bears to a bowl game last season, though he got to work in Conway before that game was played.

- **Georgia Southern Eagles** (p. 322) — There’s something to be said for an athletic department going into a college football season knowing what to expect in 2026.

- **Georgia State Panthers** (p. 324) — The Panthers got skunked in SBC action last season and their lone win was against FCS Murray State.

- **James Madison Dukes** (p. 326) — With NIL funds allocated elsewhere, the Dukes didn’t go the transfer portal route at QB, really, with the exception of UCF transfer Davi Belfort, who barely played. 247Sports gave James Madison’s portal haul the best grade in the conference by a pretty wide margin, which is good because pretty much all of last season’s production is gone, but a lot of players are from lower-division schools, FCS, or never saw the field at their P4 programs.

- **Louisiana Ragin’ Cajuns** (p. 335) — That would be Lunch Winfield, who led a four-game winning streak at the end of the regular season to get the Ragin’ Cajuns to a bowl game.

- **Louisiana Tech Bulldogs** (p. 338) — On the heels of their best season since 2019, the Bulldogs are now in the Sun Belt.
